ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit is a two-port network, with the upper left terminal as a and the lower left terminal as b. The top wire is the common upper node, and the bottom wire is connected to b. The left branch has a downward 1 A current source, with a 2 Ω resistor connected in series below it. In the middle branch, a 1 Ω resistor is connected in parallel with a voltage source labeled 2 V between the upper node and the middle node; the upper end of this 2 V voltage source is marked “−”, and the lower end is marked “+”. The middle node then is connected through a vertical 2 Ω resistor to the lower common node. The upper part of the right branch has a 2 Ω resistor, below which is connected a downward 1 A current source, and the lower end of the current source is also connected to the same lower common node; this lower common node is then connected through a 2 Ω resistor to the bottom terminal b. Reasoning: According to the specified method, let b be the reference ground, the top node be Va, the lower end of the 2 V voltage source be Vx, the upper-end node of the right-side current source be Vz, and the lower common node be Vy. From the polarity of the 2 V voltage source in the figure, Vx − Va = 2 can be obtained. Write KCL for the Vz node: the current through the upper right-side 2 Ω resistor to Va plus the downward 1 A current source current is zero, namely (Vz − Va)/2 + 1 = 0, so the current from Va to Vz through this 2 Ω resistor is 1 A. Since Vx − Va = 2, and the 1 Ω resistor is connected in parallel between Va and Vx, the 1 Ω resistor current is 2 A, with direction flowing from Vx to Va. At the top node, the left-side 1 A current source takes away 1 A downward from Va, and the upper right-side 2 Ω branch takes away 1 A rightward from Va, for a total of 2 A flowing out of Va; while the 1 Ω resistor exactly injects 2 A into Va. Therefore, the current through the 2 V voltage source is 0 A. The voltage source power P = 2 V × 0 A = 0 W.

raw_record.question_text: In the two-terminal network shown in the figure, the power of the 2 V constant voltage source is ______ W. Provide the final value as a floating-point number with one decimal place.

method.method_draft: Set b as ground. Let the top node be Va, the lower terminal of the 2 V source be Vx, the lower common node be Vy, and the node between the upper-right 2 Ω resistor and the right current source be Vz. From the voltage source polarity, impose Vx−Va=2. From KCL at Vz with the 1 A downward source, get (Vz−Va)/2+1=0, so the upper-right resistor carries 1 A from Va to Vz. From KCL at Vy and the supernode containing Va and Vx, solve the node voltages or, equivalently, evaluate KCL at Va after using Vx−Va=2: the parallel 1 Ω resistor carries 2 A from Vx up to Va, while the left current source and upper-right branch each take 1 A downward/out of Va. These currents exactly balance, so the current through the 2 V source is 0 A. Therefore its power is 2 V × 0 A = 0 W, reported as 0.0.
